name: L78L33ACUTR
title: L78L series: 100 mA positive fixed voltage regulators, 3.3 V to 24 V, in SO-8, SOT-89 and TO-92
summary: Three-terminal linear regulators for fixed positive rails from 3.3 to 24 V, delivering up to 100 mA with built-in current limiting and thermal shutdown. They come in a ±4 % A selection (AC: 0 to 125 °C junction; AB: -40 to 125 °C) and a ±8 % C selection, in SO-8, SOT-89 and TO-92. L78L33ACUTR is the 3.3 V AC part in SOT-89 on tape and reel.

circuits.title: Test circuit
circuits.description: The regulator on its own between the input and output rails, with 0.33 µF from VIN to ground and 0.1 µF from VOUT to ground. GND is the common return for both. All the electrical characteristics are measured this way.

circuits.title: High output current short-circuit protected
circuits.description: A PNP transistor Q1 carries load current alongside the regulator. Its emitter sits on VIN and its collector on VO. The regulator draws its input current IREG through a 30 Ω resistor from VIN, and the base of Q1 hangs on the regulator side of that resistor, so the drop across it is what turns Q1 on. Q1's current I(Q1) and the regulator output meet at VO. The usual 0.33 µF sits at the regulator input and 0.1 µF at the output.

circuits.title: Output boost circuit
circuits.description: The regulator's GND pin is lifted off ground by a Zener diode, so the output sits at VZ plus the regulator's own voltage VX. A resistor R from OUT to the GND pin and a 10 µF capacitor from the GND pin to ground sit on the lifted node. 0.33 µF bypasses the input and 0.1 µF the output.

circuits.title: Current regulator
circuits.description: A constant-current source. A resistor R runs from OUT to the GND pin, and the load current IO leaves from the GND pin node, so IO is the regulator voltage VX across R plus the quiescent current IQ. A capacitor C from that node to ground and 0.33 µF at the input complete it.

circuits.title: Adjustable output regulator
circuits.description: R1 from OUT to the GND pin and a variable resistor R2 from the GND pin to ground lift the regulator's reference, so turning R2 moves the output above the fixed voltage. The quiescent current IQ flows out of the GND pin into the R1-R2 junction. R2 is a potentiometer with its wiper tied to its grounded end. 0.33 µF bypasses the input and 0.1 µF the output.

operation.text: A family of three-terminal regulators for a fixed positive rail, 3.3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 15, 18 or 24 V, at up to 100 mA. Nothing outside it is needed for it to work. Named uses are local regulation on each card instead of one central regulator, higher-current regulators built round external pass transistors, and taking the place of a Zener diode and resistor, against which it offers lower quiescent current and lower noise.

An internal current limit and an over-temperature shutdown make the part very hard to destroy. Power dissipation is limited inside the part; the full 100 mA calls for enough heat sinking. Figure 6 shows the output collapsing at about 170 °C ambient with no load, and Figure 12 shows the short-circuit current peaking near 0.39 A at about 9 V across the part and falling to below 0.1 A at 35 V.

Two tolerance selections: A at ±4 % and C at ±8 %. For the 3.3 V parts at 25 °C, the A grade spans 3.168 to 3.432 V and the C grade 3.036 to 3.564 V. AB parts are specified over a junction temperature of -40 to 125 °C, AC and C parts over 0 to 125 °C.

The DC input may reach 30 V for outputs of 3.3 to 9 V, 35 V for 12 and 15 V, and 40 V for 18 and 24 V. Each output figure holds over an input span given per part: for 3.3 V, 5.3 to 20 V at 1 to 40 mA. Dropout is 1.7 V typical at 40 mA for every voltage.
The regulator works with nothing connected round it. The electrical characteristics are measured with 0.33 µF from input to ground and 0.1 µF from output to ground.

Junction to ambient is at most 200 °C/W in TO-92, and 55 °C/W in SO-8 and SOT-89 when 6 cm² of copper serves as the heat sink. Junction to case is at most 20 °C/W in SO-8 and 15 °C/W in SOT-89. In SO-8, pins 2, 3, 6 and 7 are ground and are tied inside to the die paddle; that frame lowers the thermal resistance when they connect to copper. In SOT-89 the tab is ground.

At 120 Hz and 40 mA, supply voltage rejection is 49 dB typical and 41 dB minimum for the 3.3 V parts. In Figure 10 rejection holds nearly level from 10 Hz up to roughly 20 kHz, then falls; at 100 kHz it is 6 to 8 dB below the level value.
TO-92 parts come loose in a bag, in an ammopack (suffix -AP) or on tape and reel (suffix TR). In the ammopack and reel forms the leads are formed to suit the tape.
